ic_name: NFC / ISO 14443 (NXP AN10833 MIFARE family — subset)

design_parameters.raw: - i.e. bit 2 = 1 might give a different meaning to all other

signaling_summary: ISO/IEC 14443 is fundamentally an analog/mixed-signal protocol because Layer 2 is an RF air interface. The PCD generates a 13.56 MHz unmodulated carrier at field strength H within Hmin (1.5 A/m) and Hmax (7.5 A/m); Type A PCD→PICC bits are 100% ASK Modified-Miller pulses (pause durations 2.0..3.0 μs); Type B uses 10% ASK NRZ-L. The PICC harvests power from the carrier, demodulates the envelope, and replies by switching a load resistor in/out of the resonant antenna at the 847.5 kHz subcarrier rate (Manchester for Type A, BPSK for Type B). All digital framing — bits, parity, CRC — is layered on top of this analog substrate.

voltage_classes.applicable_modes: All ISO 14443 PICCs — voltage is induced, not external.
Rectified + regulated; only valid while field is present.

type_a_pcd_to_picc_modulation.modulation_coding: Modified Miller — bit 1 = pause in second half of ETU.

type_a_picc_to_pcd_load_modulation.coding: Manchester — bit 1 = subcarrier ON in first half ETU + OFF in second half.

type_b_pcd_to_picc_modulation.modulation_coding: NRZ-L — high amplitude carrier = bit 1, lower amplitude = bit 0; each ETU carries one bit.

notes: The PICC analog front-end is a passive rectifier + shunt regulator + envelope detector + load-switch modulator with no analog trim register exposed to the air interface — vendor-specific trim is wafer-test programmed and not visible to the PCD over RF.
evidence_in_an10833: Section 1.3: 'The ISO/IEC 14443-2 defines the carrier frequency of 13.56 MHz, the modulation, and the bit coding'
